No. It's an FSPS bookkeeping label, not a physical line.

- **NIST ASD** lists no O II line near 3867 Å in air. Between 3860 and 3875 Å the only entries are allowed lines at 3863.5, 3864.1, 3864.4, 3864.7, 3872.4 and 3874.1 Å. Source: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASD/lines1.pl?spectra=O+II&low_w=3860&upp_w=3875
- **FSPS** carries it as "[O II] 3867" at 3868.16 Å vacuum in `data/emlines_info.dat`, but its flux is exactly zero in all 770 models of the Cloudy grid `nebular/ZAU_ND_mist.lines`. The neighbouring [Ne III] 3869 column is non-zero everywhere.
- Ceridwen already drops it via `EXCLUDED_LINES` in `ceridwen/ceridwen/likelihood/emission_lines.py:88`, keeping [Ne III] 3869 as the real line there.

I did not trace which Cloudy label produced the entry.
